result:
Solution 1 is wrong: 14400 is the Hill number, the conjectured topological crossing number, which pseudolinear drawings cannot reach. The count it uses, e_k = 3(k+1) for all k ≤ 14, is not achievable for n = 33. The simple bound E_{≤k} ≥ 3·C(k+2,2) already gives about 0.375·C(33,4) ≈ 15,000 crossings. Even the rectilinear crossing number of K_33 is above 14,400. I recall it as roughly 14,600, which is a recollection, not a derivation.

Solution 2 is wrong: it assumes that every choice of one vertex from each of four vertex-orbits gives a crossing. That would force about 26,730 of the 40,920 possible 4-subsets to be convex, a ratio of about 0.65, far above the roughly 0.36–0.38 that good drawings achieve. Its claim that this is the minimum is unsupported.

Solution 3 gives 15834 without any actual derivation; the optimization step is only asserted. That is a ratio of about 0.387 to C(33,4). This seems too high for the minimum, because 3-symmetric constructions come close to the rectilinear value for n = 33, which I recall as about 14,600. This verdict rests on that recalled estimate and not on a computed value.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
